html:
The Pamir Highway is a road across the Pamir mountains of Tajikistan, linking Osh in Kyrgyzstan with Khorog and Dushanbe, built by the Soviets in the 1930s. It crosses passes of over 4,600 metres, among the highest roads in the world.

The Pamirs had been a border zone of the Great Game, where the Russian and British empires met; the thin Wakhan strip of Afghanistan was left to keep them apart. The road let the Soviets supply garrisons and bring the remote valleys under control.

Most people along it are Pamiris, who speak eastern Iranian languages and follow the Ismaili branch of Shia Islam, led by the Aga Khan. In the civil war his aid convoys along the highway kept the region from famine. Today it is a trade route to China and a famous trip for cyclists and drivers.
